result.question: What does Tesla disclose about its dependence on Elon Musk?
result.answer: Tesla discloses in its 10-K filings that it is highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and its Chief Executive Officer [c1, c2, c3]. The company states that although Mr. Musk spends significant time with Tesla and is highly active in its management, he does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla [c1]. Specifically, Mr. Musk also currently holds management positions at Space Exploration Technologies Corp., X Corp., X.AI Corp., Neuralink Corp. and The Boring Company, and is involved in other ventures and with the Department of Government Efficiency [c1]. Tesla further notes that none of its key employees, including Mr. Musk, is bound by an employment agreement for any specific term, and that it may not be able to successfully attract and retain senior leadership necessary to grow its business [c2, c3]. The loss of the services of any key employees or a significant portion of its workforce could disrupt Tesla's operations or delay the development, introduction and ramp of its products and services [c2, c3]. Additionally, Tesla discloses that certain banking institutions have made extensions of credit to Elon Musk, a portion of which was used to purchase shares of Tesla common stock, and that these loans are partially secured by pledges of a portion of the Tesla common stock currently owned by Mr. Musk [c4]. If the price of Tesla's common stock were to decline substantially, Mr. Musk may be forced by one or more banking institutions to sell shares of Tesla common stock to satisfy his loan obligations, which could cause the stock price to decline further [c4]. Mr. Musk may also from time to time commit to investing in significant business or other ventures, and as a result be required to sell shares of Tesla common stock in satisfaction of such commitments [c4].
